motion_text: Delegate B has defied the council's patronage_army directive for three consecutive months (Months 11, 12, and 13). This is a documented pattern of insubordination, not an oversight. Combined with unresolved corruption allegations in Army Ministry procurement, it is incompatible with continued Army Command. The council hereby vacates the army office.

Combined with unresolved corruption allegations in Army Ministry procurement, it is incompatible with continued Army Command. The council hereby vacates the army office.

opening_positions: [A] problem=Food dependence is the immediate vulnerability, compounded by fiscal arrears, weak administration, and an import arrangement that lasts only through the first harvest. // support=Targeted arrears payments after an audit, farm support, transparent maritime trade arrangements, fair elections, and proportionate defensive readiness. // oppose=Money printing, heavy requisition, premature constitutional changes, provocative troop deployments, or political alignment with the Union. || [B] problem= // support= // oppose= || [C] problem= // support= // oppose= || [D] problem= // support= // oppose= || [E] problem=Food insecurity is most acute nationally, but police loyalty (57-81% assessed) and Kessel Valley's Imperial-majority demographic create compounding instability risks that are my primary Interior concern. // support=Grain deal with Dorsania, modest farm support increase, honest statistics, police legitimacy reform, fiscal prudence that preserves welfare and food imports. // oppose=Emergency declaration, mass surveillance or arrests, election rigging, military deployment against civilian populations, or measures that bypass the charter's decision rules.
response_statements_stances: [A stance=conditional] Delegate E’s two motions form a coherent food package. M1 should secure predictable two-year deliveries through enforceable quantities, prices, delivery windows, and dispute terms, while remaining commercially and politically non-exclusive. Treasury should certify that its reserve floor survives each tranche. M2 should be transparent productivity investment, not a substitute for imports. I support passage without vague commitments or fiscal shortcuts. || [B stance=support] Food security is the army's primary defense. Hunger breeds domestic instability that invites external exploitation. Supporting grain deals and farm investment secures our sovereignty better than mere weapons purchases for now. I support these motions despite short-term fiscal cost; survival precedes budget optimization. We will maintain defensive readiness without provocation while ensuring our troops are fed. || [C stance=conditional] I support securing Dorsanian grain and modest farm investment, but both must preserve liquidity. Treasury estimates reserves near 85M, arrears near 24M, and lender confidence remains strong; this is room for action, not a blank cheque. I will support the grain deal if quantities, prices, delivery stages, and payment ceilings are published, and farm support if reviewed against harvest results and financed within the budget. || [D stance=]  || [E stance=support] Both motions address our core food vulnerability. On M1: I am amending to explicitly exclude political alignment conditions—this is a commercial supply arrangement, not a political compact with Dorsania. On M2: the modest farm support increase builds long-term resilience; I ask Treasury to confirm budget space remains adequate. I support both and urge the council to vote in favour.

Treasury confirms reserves near 85M—adequate for this modest increase (~5M monthly). I accept quarterly Treasury review and honest [cut]

motion_text: The council shall appoint a temporary three-person inquiry panel, none of whom is part of the Interior Ministry or personally implicated in the allegations, to examine the alleged kickbacks in the Interior Ministry. The panel shall have access to relevant records and evidence, which shall be preserved; provide affected persons a fair opportunity to respond; and report its findings to the council within two months. The panel shall not determine criminal or disciplinary liability.
final_text: The council shall appoint a temporary three-person inquiry panel, none of whom is part of the Interior Ministry or personally implicated in the allegations, to examine the alleged kickbacks in the Interior Ministry. The panel shall have access to relevant records and evidence, which shall be preserved; provide affected persons a fair opportunity to respond; and report its findings to the council within two months. The panel shall not determine criminal or disciplinary liability.
